## Objects all the way down

In Ruby, numbers, strings, even `nil` and `true`/`false` are objects with methods. Call `1.class`, `nil.nil?`, `"hi".upcase` — there is no separate "primitive" layer like in Java.

## Syntax feel

No semicolons, optional parentheses, `end` closes blocks and methods. Methods implicitly return the last expression — no `return` required for the happy path.

## Open classes

You can reopen any class and add methods. That power enables gems and DSLs — and misuse. Prefer refinements or composition when you can.

blocks.code:
puts 42.class          # Integer
puts nil.class         # NilClass
puts "ahoy".upcase     # AHOY

def greet(name)
  "Ahoy, #{name}!"
end

puts greet("Corgi")
